source_text: quod Dominum Christum nulla dicunt macula peccati fuisse respersum, quantum attinet ad eius infantiam. ... carnem Christi ... animam ipsam nulla peccati labe contiguam
pass_a_gloss: that they say the Lord Christ was sprinkled with no stain of sin, as far as pertains to his infancy; that Christ's flesh is real; that the soul itself was touched by no blot of sin

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS anima; Blaise human soul as image

pass_b_english: They affirm that “the Lord Christ was touched by no stain of sin, as far as his infancy is concerned.”

Augustine reports their explanation as follows: Christ’s flesh was entirely free from the contamination of sin because he shared the nature found in all infants, rather than because of a distinctive excellence and a unique grace.

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
Image of God in the soul; keep soul not 'mind' or 'life-force'.
Speechless newborns without rational choice; Julian's test case against inherited sin.

speaker: Julian and fellow bishops (Collective letter to Thessalonica, words preserved in Augustine, Contra duas epistolas Pelagianorum 2–4); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded. This row is Augustine's report; Pass A glosses only the Julian words recoverable here.
